processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: A 39 kg low-density steel ingot with the composition Fe-0.25C-3Mn-2Al-0.4Si-0.009S-0.009P was produced via vacuum induction melting.
The ingot was hot forged and cut into billets measuring 90 mm (length) × 70 mm (width) × 40 mm (thickness).
Billets were heated to 1200 °C and held for 60 min prior to hot rolling.

Hot rolling was carried out on a high-rigidity two-roll mill, beginning at 1100 °C, involving six passes with a cumulative reduction rate of 90%, yielding plates with a final thickness of 4 mm; finish rolling completed at 880 °C followed by air cooling.
Cold rolling was performed on a four-roll reversible mill with a 60% reduction rate, resulting in plates with a thickness of 1.6 mm.
The cold-rolled samples were annealed at 750 °C for 30 min within the critical region and air-cooled to room temperature, labeled AN750.
The AN750 samples underwent low bainite aging by holding at 400 °C for 30 min, producing samples designated AN750-T.

structures.overall_structure: Multiphase heterogeneous microstructure composed of ferrite (F), bainite/tempered martensite (B/TM), fresh martensite (FM), and retained austenite (RA); after deformation, deformation-induced martensite (DIM) forms via the TRIP effect.

phases_present.morphology: lath/sheaf bainite and tempered martensite; carbides inside bainite at 60° to boundaries
blocky/lath fresh martensite; islands of FM+RA

defects.dislocation_density: Initial dislocation densities ρ0: F 0.33×10^14 m^-2; B/TM 0.44×10^14 m^-2; FM 0.86×10^14 m^-2; RA 0.81×10^14 m^-2

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: Heterogeneous/bimodal: F ≈ 4.53 µm, B/TM ≈ 1.73 µm, FM ≈ 1.06 µm, RA ≈ 0.57 µm.

precipitates.distribution: Carbides inside bainitic ferrite are distributed at a 60° angle to its boundaries; in tempered martensite, carbides are randomly distributed.

phases_present.morphology: strain-induced martensite transformed from retained austenite via the TRIP effect
retained austenite partially consumed by strain-induced transformation

defect_interactions.interaction_type: GND accumulation at soft/hard phase boundaries
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Strain gradients at F/B-TM-FM interfaces cause geometrically necessary dislocation accumulation; KAM peaks when the characteristic line crosses the boundary and then decreases (KAM_AVE = 0.53° for AN750-T), generating back stress opposite to the applied stress.
During deformation, RA transforms into DIM (final DIM fraction 4.74%), enhancing strain-hardening capacity and local strength.

interfaces.slip_behavior: Coordinated deformation between soft ferrite and hard domains; the soft domain hardens while the hard domain softens, maintaining deformation continuity. No Lüders bands or Portevin-Le Chatelier bands were observed.
interfaces.phase_evolution: RA transforms into DIM during deformation via the TRIP effect; RA drops from 7.4% (before deformation) to 1.8% in the necking region after fracture, while DIM reaches 4.74%.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Load applied parallel to the rolling direction (RD); DIC images captured every 2 s during deformation.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Yield strength relative to conventional low-alloy high-strength steels

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: field emission Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM), FEI Quanta-650 FEG
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: etched with 4% nitric acid ethanol solution
characterization_methods.key_findings: AN750-T shows F and B with islands labelled FM+RA.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: 20 kV operating voltage, scanning step size 0.2 µm, minimum pixel size 9; BCC and FCC indexed
characterization_methods.purpose: Phase distribution, image quality (IQ) separation of FM/B-TM/F, and KAM strain analysis
characterization_methods.key_findings: AN750-T: FCC 0.074 / BCC 0.926; IQ FM 39532.6, IQ B/TM 64306.6; IQ histogram Peak I 41750, Peak II 71477, Ave 63161; KAM_AVE = 0.53°.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Tecnai G2 F20 transmission electron microscope, 200 kV
characterization_methods.purpose: Examine dislocation and substructure evolution; distinguish bainite from tempered martensite via carbide orientation
characterization_methods.key_findings: AN750-T BF TEM shows regions labelled TM, F and B; carbides inside bainite at 60° to boundaries, randomly distributed in TM; RA identified with SAED along [110]γ.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: JEOL JXA-8230 Electron Probe Microanalyzer, 15 kV, working current 5 × 10^-8 A
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine elemental distribution within the microstructure
characterization_methods.key_findings: Carbon is mainly concentrated in B/TM, FM, and RA; in AN750-T the C profile shows marked maxima aligned with B, RA and FM bands while Si, Al and Mn stay nearly flat.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: accelerating voltage 40 kV, tube current 40 mA, scanning angle 30°–110°, rolling plane
characterization_methods.key_findings: γ reflections (γ(200), γ(220), γ(311)) confirm retained austenite in AN750-T.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Instron 3382 testing machine; Digital Image Correlation system
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature, strain rate 5 × 10^-4 s^-1, GB/T 228.1—2021, load parallel to RD, DIC images every 2 s
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure tensile properties and monitor local strain distribution
characterization_methods.key_findings: AN750-T: yield strength 697 MPa, tensile strength 1068 MPa, elongation 34.0%; relatively uniform strain in the yield stage with stress redistribution during uniform plastic deformation.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: SEM; Nano Measure software for dimple size statistics
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize crack path and dimple statistics in the necking region after tensile fracture
characterization_methods.key_findings: AN750-T shows relatively deep dimples; bimodal dimple size distribution with Ave = 1.54 µm, Peak I = 0.72 µm, Peak II = 2.26 µm.

computational_details.simulation_method: Constitutive model combining the iso-work theory and the von Mises equivalent method
computational_details.software_used: AZtecCrystal (Parent Grain Analysis module) for RA/DIM parent-grain reconstruction
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Initial phase fractions: F 49.3%, B/TM 35.0%, FM 8.3%, RA 7.4% (f_RA,0 = 7.4%); Olson-Cohen parameters α = 5, β = 1.28, n = 0.55; ν = 0.28.
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Model fits experimental data well; calculated values are higher at the initial strain stage; at necking strain the maximum back stress σ_B = 217 MPa, while the GND-induced back stress strengthening contribution is 236 MPa.

analytical_models.equation_role: Distributes tensile work uniformly across phases (σ_F dε_F = σ_B/TM dε_B/TM = σ_FM dε_FM = σ_RA dε_RA = σ_DIM dε_DIM)
analytical_models.model_note: Used to analyze the mechanical behavior of each phase during deformation.

analytical_models.equation_role: Fits the strain-induced martensite transformation: f_DIM = f_RA,0{1 - exp[-β(1 - exp(-αε))^n]}

analytical_models.model_note: Applied to F and RA; grain sizes taken from Fig. 6(b).
Phase-resolved Taylor factor, shear modulus, Burgers vector and ρ0 for AN750-T are listed in Table A2.

analytical_models.equation_role: dρ_j = M_j(1/(b_j Λ_j) + k_j^1/b_j √ρ_j - k_j^2 ρ_j) dε_j
analytical_models.model_note: Mean free path equals average phase size for F, B/TM, FM; RA mean free path modified by DIM transformation.
R and Δh from Table A2; c from parent grain analysis; back stress is added to the flow stress summation.

unmapped_findings: Critical transformation temperatures of the experimental steel (dilatometry, tangent method): Ac1 = 705 °C, Ac3 = 950 °C, Bf = 380 °C, Ms = 346 °C.
Product of strength and elongation (PSE) of AN750-T reaches 36.3 GPa %.
Maximum back stress (σ_B) at necking strain for AN750-T = 217 MPa; the GND-induced back stress strengthening contribution at necking = 236 MPa.
B/TM contributes about 23% of the flow stress at necking strain in AN750-T.
Dimple size statistics for AN750-T (central fracture zone): average 1.54 µm, bimodal peaks at 0.72 µm and 2.26 µm; AN750-T shows relatively deep dimples.
After tensile fracture, the retained austenite fraction in the AN750-T necking region decreased to 0.018 (1.8%); point-to-point orientation average P-T-P_AVE = 3.50.
No dynamic propagation instabilities such as Lüders bands or Portevin-Le Chatelier bands were observed in any samples, including AN750-T.
In AN750-T, the crack tip blunts at the hard domain interface and generates secondary cracks during tensile fracture.
